_schema: Program control file, owned by Coach Claude, edited via GitHub — the app applies it on next launch with no rebuild. Keyed by app id. PER-EXERCISE FIELDS: name (display; history/Airtable key on the id, renames safe), sr (header target label, keep short), equipment / setup / execute / note (card copy), session ('U1'/'L1'/'U2'/'L2' — MOVES the exercise to that session), removed (true DETACHES it; delete the flag to bring it back; its history is preserved), and meta {n, lo, hi, inc, unit, ph, vm, rest, pain, bw, deg, bar, mus, maxw} — n is SET COUNT (rows rebuild to match), unit 'reps'|'sec', ph = per-hand, vm volume multiplier, rest seconds, pain = elbow buttons, bw bodyweight, deg angle-logged, bar = bar weight for plate math, mus = heat-map muscles, maxw = load ceiling (red warn + toast, never blocks). next {w, r, asof 'YYYY-MM-DD', why} PINS the next-session target over the app's computed suggestion (shows on the card as 'coach: <why>'; REQUIRES asof and expires once the exercise is banked on/after it; maxw still caps; delete the block or let it expire to return to computed). ADDING AN EXERCISE: create a NEW id whose first two characters are the session slot (a1/a2/b1/b2 = U1/L1/U2/L2, e.g. 'a2X') or set session explicitly, give it at least name + meta {n, lo, hi} + setup/execute — the app renders a full working card (no diagram); ALSO create its Exercises record in Airtable with App ID = the new id so webhook syncs link. Top-level _arms: {"A1": [ids], "A2": [ids]} sets which exercises belong to the optional arms blocks (defaults: A1 = a18/a19/a16 from U1, A2 = b15/b19/b18 from U2). ONE merged Arms tab renders whatever is pending — one block, the other, or both interleaved bi/tri as a single arms day — and everything when nothing is pending; done blocks hide behind a 'show anyway' link. Standalone runs bank as session 'Arms'; the U1/U2 toggle folds a block into its parent for the day. History keys on exercise ids so progression never forks; a17/b17 (wrist extensor rehab) are ALWAYS excluded whatever this lists. Top-level _bw: [{d:'YYYY-MM-DD', w, bf, lean}, ...] pushes body-comp readings into the app's bodyweight log (coach's value wins on a duplicate date; omit bf/lean when unrecorded — blank never means zero); feeds the Goals card, recomp chart, rolling average and weigh-in reminder; to CORRECT a reading write a new row for the same date (deleting a row does not un-merge an already-applied value). Top-level _order: {"U1": [ids…], …} reorders within a session (listed first, rest follow); keys "A1"/"A2"/"Arms" are BLOCK orders for the arms tab (single-block and merged-day layouts) and never touch U1/U2. To move an exercise into or out of an arms block use _arms, not the per-id session field. Top-level _goal: {date, weight, bf, lean, baselineDate, baselineWeight, baselineBf, baselineLean, note} renders the Goals card at the top of the Log tab — lean is a FLOOR (hold or gain), baselines are the progress-bar starting points, note shows verbatim under the bars; rewrite the whole block at each new horizon, delete it to hide the card. Top-level _weighin: {everyDays, pauseUntil 'YYYY-MM-DD'} drives the weigh-in cadence line on the Bodyweight card ('last weigh-in N days ago', amber 'weigh-in due' at everyDays, quiet dot on the Log button) — factual and dismissible only, never streaks or red; pauseUntil silences it through that date (travel, protocol changes); delete the block to turn the reminder off. Top-level _next: {code, asof} overrides the rotation pointer, expiring once that session is banked on/after asof. STILL BUILD-ONLY: new session TYPES beyond the four, webhook/hosting changes. Blank/omitted fields fall back to baked text. Bad JSON is ignored safely.

b16.setup: Anchors at height 21 (confirmed 8/14). Step back until there is tension before rep one.
b16.note: Well-suited to the Ancore: resistance rises as the cable extends, which peaks the load right at the squeeze - exactly where rear delts want it. No distance adjustment needed.

next.why: hold — rear delts do not need more load

a17.note:
CHANGED 9/17: this was a wrist EXTENSOR eccentric (palm down) for two months. Josh localised the pain to the INNER elbow — the medial epicondyle, where the wrist FLEXORS and pronators originate. Extensor work was treating the wrong tendon. Palm UP from here.

HARD CEILING 5 LB. Rehab, not training — controlled, sub-maximal, never to failure, never past Med. This is the medicine that keeps the elbow trainable. If 5x15 ever feels genuinely trivial, the next step is 7.5, and only after two clean weeks.

Medial also explains the history better than lateral did: grip comes from the finger flexors, which originate here — so the 8/4 twinge after gripping a pulldown bar, and the long-standing bench-press trigger, both fit. Worth confirming with a physio rather than building further on inference.

next.why: ceiling — rehab, never past Med

a17.name: Wrist FLEXOR Eccentric
a17.equipment: One dumbbell, 5 lb · forearm supported on a bench or your thigh, PALM UP
a17.setup: Forearm flat and supported, palm facing UP, wrist just past the edge. Dumbbell in that hand.
a17.execute: Let the weight lower your wrist back toward the floor over 3 SECONDS — that slow lowering is the whole exercise. Use your OTHER hand to lift it back to the start. Only the lowering is loaded.

a23.note: RIGHT KNEE WATCH. Josh reported knee pressure at 30 lb on 9/8 and said do not add weight — that call stands and outranks the completed rep range. This is the heaviest kneecap loader in the program and the knee is a managed constraint, so it does not climb on rep count alone. Progress with reps and a hard squeeze at the top. b22.setup: Rear foot on a LOWER platform than before (8/11 knee flag), laces flat / tops of toes down, pad under the foot if the bench edge digs. Long stance, front shin vertical.
b22.note: RIGHT KNEE WATCH: pain during reps with the RIGHT foot as the REAR (elevated) leg, 8/11. Rear-leg pain is deep-flexion pressure — the platform height is the first fix. If it still talks after the lower setup, the slot swaps to lateral lunge or goblet box squat (reverse lunge already occupies b25). Report honestly rather than pushing through.

a14.setup: Ancore anchors at chest height. STEP WELL FORWARD - far enough that the cables are already under real tension with your arms open wide, before rep one.
a14.note: DISTANCE MATTERS ON THIS ONE (8/16): Ancore resistance RISES as the cable extends, so the stretch position - arms wide, where the chest actually grows - is where tension is lowest. Standing farther from the units restores load in the stretch. If the wide position feels loose, you are standing too close, regardless of the number on the plates.

next.why: 14x3 clean — first Ancore increase

a19.setup: One Ancore at HIP HEIGHT behind you. Face away, working arm trailing behind the body, palm forward, one arm at a time. STEP FORWARD until the cable is tight with the arm hanging back - tension must exist at the bottom.
a19.note: This exercise exists to load the biceps long head in the STRETCH (arm behind the body). Ancore tension rises as the cable extends, which works against that - so the step-forward distance is doing the work the weight number cannot. Set up so the stretched bottom position already feels loaded. Numbers are actual pounds. Stop 15-20 degrees short of full extension.

next.why: 15x15 after 10 felt Easy — 15 is the right load

b18.note: Well-suited to the Ancore: load peaks at lockout, where the triceps are shortest - the curve matches the exercise. Stop short of hard lockout for the elbow.

next.why: range topped at 10

a28.name: Pallof Press  (anti-rotation)
a28.equipment: One Ancore at CHEST height · single handle
a28.setup: ANCHOR HEIGHT 18 (confirmed 9/20). Stand side-on to the anchor, feet shoulder-width. Step out until the cable is already under tension before rep one. Handle at your sternum, both hands.
a28.execute: Press the handle straight out until your arms are extended, resisting the cable’s pull to rotate you. Hold 2 seconds at full extension, return slowly. Hips and shoulders stay square — the point is that NOTHING moves. All reps one side, then switch.
a28.note: The missing plane. Push, pull, squat, hinge, carry and side-bend were all covered; rotation was not — which is why twisting is where you feel tight. Anti-rotation comes first: you learn to own the range before loading it. The Ancore’s rising curve SUITS this one — tension peaks at full extension, exactly where the anti-rotation demand is highest, so no need to stand extra far back. Start at 10 lb; if your torso twists, it’s too heavy.

next.why: hold 25 — set 2 was Hard. Own 12 first

b28.name: Cable Chop  (rotation)
b28.equipment: One Ancore mounted HIGH (face height or above) · rope or single handle
b28.setup: Stand side-on to the anchor, feet wider than shoulders. Both hands on the attachment at your high shoulder.
b28.execute: Pull down and across your body toward the opposite hip, rotating through the MID-BACK. Control the return over 3 seconds — the eccentric is where the range gets built. All reps one side, then switch.
b28.note: Loaded rotation — the counterpart to the Pallof press. Rotation belongs in the thoracic spine (~35° per side); the lumbar spine is built to resist it (~5–13° total). If you feel this in your LOW BACK, you’re rotating from the wrong place — cut the range and the weight. Rope beats a bar here: your wrists rotate freely through the arc, which the elbow prefers. Start at 10 lb.

next.why: 10 was Easy — 15 both sides now

b29.name: Kneeling Cable Crunch
b29.equipment: Rack lat tower, high pulley · rope
b29.setup: Kneel facing the stack, rope behind your head, hands holding it at your ears. Hips stay put — they do not travel back as you crunch.
b29.execute: Curl your RIBS toward your HIPS, rounding the spine — this is a short movement, not a bow. The hips stay fixed; if they hinge backward it becomes a lat pulldown with your abs along for the ride. Squeeze 1 second at the bottom, return over 3.
b29.note: The only spinal-FLEXION work in the program — everything else is anti-extension (ab wheel), anti-rotation (Pallof), rotation (chop), or lateral (QL raise, carry). Honest framing: visible abs come from body fat, not ab volume. This adds thickness underneath; the recomp does the rest. Numbers are relative to the lat tower carriage, not comparable to dumbbells.

next.why: top the range at 30 before adding

a13.note:
THE LIGHT PULL. Deliberately separated from the U2 heavy pulldown on 9/9 — they had converged to within 5 lb and become the same exercise twice a week. This one is moderate load for 12–15 reps, on the day you also press three times. It also sits on the day your elbow historically complained (8/4 twinge came from pulldowns after pressing), so keeping load off it here is deliberate.

a15.note: NECK: you have documented cervical stenosis (2022 MRI — severe foraminal narrowing at C5-C6 and C6-C7). STOP AT SHOULDER HEIGHT. Going above it shifts the work to the upper traps, which is the opposite of what a cranky neck wants.

a16.note: NEW ATTACHMENT 9/4 — rotating V-grip replaces the fixed Rogue bar. The swivel lets your wrists find their own angle through the rep instead of being locked pronated, which is the single cheapest elbow upgrade available on this movement. Keep 25 lb for the first session and judge the FEEL, not the number: if the elbow is quieter, that is the attachment doing its job. Elbows stay pinned to your sides; stop just short of hard lockout.

a1a.name: Face Pull / Rear Delt Fly
a1a.equipment: Ancore cables, anchor height 21 · rope or dual handles
a1a.setup: Anchors at height 21. Step back until there is tension before rep one.
a1a.execute: Pull toward your face, elbows high and wide, externally rotating so your hands finish beside your ears. Squeeze the rear delts and mid-back at the end. Slow return.
a1a.note: ADDED 9/20 for the neck and shoulders. This is the single best exercise in the program for cervical and scapular support, and U1 had none — it was only in U2. Builds the posterior shoulder and mid-back that hold your head and shoulders in a better position. Well matched to the Ancore curve: tension peaks at the squeeze, which is where rear delts want it. Same movement as b16; progress them together.

next.why: match your U2 face pull

a25.note: MOVED TO FIRST 9/20. This is two jobs in one slot: the ROCKS are ankle mobility, the RAISES are calf strength. Ankle dorsiflexion is the most common limiter of squat depth, so doing the mobility half before squatting directly improves the squat - that is worth more than the small cost of squatting on slightly pre-fatigued calves at these loads. Do the rocks deliberately through full range before the raises.
